why: Text FORCE_CONSTANTS export formats every 3-vector in a Python loop. On a 3x3x3 supercell of example/NaCl (216 atoms, 186625 lines) the median of 7 calls is 200.225 ms and the full spread is 1.65% of that median. Writing the same text with fewer Python calls should clear 20%. Open PRs do not change this function; #778 only adds neighboring HDF5 helpers. This is not the vasprun parser from #1085.

The text FORCE_CONSTANTS reader is readline plus float() per number. Parsing the same 3x3x3 NaCl file (9704457 bytes) takes a median 129.264 ms over 7 calls, spread 1.39%. A bulk parse that returns the same array should clear 20%. No open issue or PR edits this parser; #778 adds a separate HDF5 force-sets reader.

mesh.yaml with eigenvectors is built one line at a time in nested Python loops. example/Al2O3 (30 atoms) on a Gamma-centered 4x4x4 mesh with eigenvectors writes 28459636 bytes at a median 424.966 ms over 7 calls, spread 1.76%. Formatting the same YAML with fewer Python calls should clear 20%. No open PR or issue touches Mesh.write_yaml; #644 is a GPU q-point path.

The --fc-spg-symmetry kernel rotates the full force-constant tensor once per space-group operation and scatters it with fancy indexing. A 2x2x2 supercell of example/NaCl (64 atoms, 1536 operations) takes a median 1104.928 ms over 7 calls, spread 1.35%. Dropping the per-operation temporaries should clear 20% and leave the averaged tensor unchanged. The CLI already warns that this step may take some time. No open PR or issue covers this function.
